what: RI Church St Solar, LLC (Ontario, California) asks for a major change to its already-approved solar energy facility plan at 391 Church Street, Wood River Junction. The agenda doesn't say what the changes are.

who: RI Church St Solar, LLC, 401 S. Doubleday Avenue, Ontario, CA (applicant/owner)

line: Changes to the approved solar farm at 391 Church St: board may vote

Doubleday Avenue, Ontario, CA 91761 (applicant/owner) for proposed changes to an approved solar energy facility plan for property located at 391 Church Street, Wood River Junction, RI 02894 (Assessor’s Plat 11A, Lot 5). what: Charbert Solar 3, LLC wants to build a 4.5 MW AC (5.625 MW DC) solar farm at 299 Church Street, Wood River Junction, on land owned by F & E Enterprises, LLC. This is a pre-application review; no votes will be taken.
where: 299 Church Street, Wood River Junction, RI 02894 (Assessor's Plat 11A, Lot 6)
who: Charbert Solar 3, LLC, 260 West Exchange Street, Providence (applicant); F & E Enterprises, LLC, 160 Plainfield Street, Providence (owner)
next: No vote. A formal application would come later; the agenda doesn't give a date.
history: Also on the Sep 24 Planning Board agenda (pre-application).
line: 4.5 MW solar farm proposed at 299 Church St: early review, no vote
quote: for a proposed 4.5 MW AC/5.625 MW DC solar energy facility for property located at 299 Church Street, Wood River Junction, RI 02894 (Assessor’s Plat 11A, Lot 6). The Planning Board will discuss and consider the applicant’s Pre-Application submission, but no votes will be taken.

what: Ordinance O-2 sets out the uses allowed by special use permit in the Rural Business zoning district. The list includes telecom antennas attached to existing structures, along with offices, vet hospitals, restaurants and others. The agenda doesn't say what is new in the list.
where: Rural Business Zoning District (townwide zoning, Sec. 32-166)
next: First reading only. The agenda's other zoning item shows the pattern: a public hearing comes at second reading. No date is given.
line: Rural Business zone use list, including cell antennas on existing buildings: 1st reading
quote: O-2 Chapter 32-ZONING, Article XXVIII.-Rural Business Zoning District, Sec. 32-166.-Permitted Uses. (1st reading) All uses permitted within the rural business district shall require a special use permit, unless otherwise indicated.

what: The council votes on hiring RISE Group, Inc. of Cranston to design and build a solar carport at the town's Highway Facility: $1,518,022 base, plus $61,671 for U.S.-made equipment, plus a 5% contingency, for a total not to exceed $1,658,677.65.
who: RISE Group, Inc., 1341 Elmwood Avenue, Cranston, RI (contractor); Town Manager (award)
next: If approved, the award still depends on contract talks, confirmed financing, the Town Solicitor's approval of the documents, and the contractor's bonds and insurance.
line: Town votes on a $1.66 million contract for a solar carport at the highway garage
quote: to award a Design-Build contract to RISE Group, Inc., 1341 Elmwood Avenue, Cranston, Rhode Island 02910, for the design, permitting, procurement, construction, utility interconnection, commissioning and closeout of the Highway Facility Solar Carport Project, in the base amount of One Million Five Hundred Eighteen Thousand Twenty-Two Posted on 10/08/2026 5 Dollars ($1,518,022)

what: The council proposes a new zoning section (610) with a 'form-based code' for the Old Tower Hill Road area: five new districts with rules aimed at a walkable, mixed-use neighborhood, plus when the rules apply and how projects get reviewed.
where: Old Tower Hill Road area (five Form-Based Districts on the Regulating Plan Map)
next: The hearing continues from Sep 14 and Sep 28. The council can vote after it closes; no date is given.
history: Also on the Sep 14 (hearing opened) and Sep 28 (continued) Town Council agendas; the Planning Board followed up Oct 6. Resident emails for and against are in this agenda’s communications.
line: Old Tower Hill Road form-based zoning: hearing continues from Sep 14 and Sep 28
quote: A. A Public Hearing, continued from September 14 and September 28, 2026, to consider proposed amendments to the Zoning Ordinance, Appendix A: Article 6, New Section 610, to implement Old Tower Hill Road Form-Based Code (FBC) and establish five (5) Form-Based Districts, as shown on the attached Regulating Plan Map

what: Ordinance 2026-8 would change the zoning map for Assessor's Plat 43, Lots 264 and 265 on Shun Pike from R-40 (residential) to I-Industrial. It began as a petition by Bachar Sasa (2025-CP-10). The agenda doesn't say what would be built.
next: The council may vote the same night ('Votes may be taken on any or all items'). Unfinished business after 10:30 pm carries to the fourth Monday.
history: Sep 14 Town Council agenda: petition 2025-CP-10 by Bachar Sasa for the same lots, referred to the Planning Board for an advisory opinion.

what: Solicitor Marcello updates the council on other ways to resolve a possible PFAS moratorium. This agenda doesn't say what the moratorium would stop. what: The city proposes zoning changes to allow cannabis retail stores by special use permit in the C-2 through C-5 and I-1 through I-3 districts, and cannabis growing, manufacturing and testing labs in the I-1 through I-3 districts, with safety standards and minimum distances from certain uses. The Planning Board decides what to recommend to the City Council.
where: Citywide (C-2, C-3, C-4, C-5, I-1, I-2 & I-3 districts)
next: The recommendation goes to the City Council.
line: Cannabis shops and growers zoning: Planning Board advises City Council, may vote
quote: Changes proposed would amend the Zoning Ordinance to allow cannabis retail establishments by special use permit in the C-2, C-3, C-4, C-5, I-1, I-2 & I-3 districts, and allow cannabis cultivation, manufacturing establishments and testing laboratories in the I-1, I-2 & I-3 districts. Special use permit criteria are included with safety standards and minimum distance requirements from certain uses.
